fact_en: Meat-eating animals have sharp, pointed teeth built for tearing and cutting through flesh.
fact_bis: Ang mga hayop nga mokaon og karne adunay hait nga ngipon nga gigamit sa paggisi ug pagputol sa unod.

findings.note: title_bis "Matarong nga Ngipon sa Karniboro" — matarong = righteous/upright, not sharp; the body correctly says "hait nga ngipon". Title-only, but it describes carnivore teeth as straight/proper rather than sharp. Same swap at ffct-13345 ("The Sharp Fovea" -> "Fovea Matarong") and ffct-32728 ("Sharp Obsidian Glass" -> "Obsidian nga Matarong").

fact_en: The spine protects the spinal cord, the bundle of nerves that connects your brain to the rest of your body.
fact_bis: Ang bukog sa likod nanalipod sa spinal cord, ang hugpong sa mga nerbiyo nga nagsumpay sa utok ngadto sa tibuok lawas.

findings.note: title_bis "Gulugod Protekta sa Utok" = "the spine protects the brain" — false; the skull protects the brain. EN title and the body both say spinal cord, and every other spinal-cord card in the corpus keeps gulugod/taludtod/spinal cord (ffct-07231, ffct-08014, ffct-09897). Title states a wrong fact on its own.

fact_en: The whale shark is an endangered animal, so we must protect it and never destroy its home.
fact_bis: Ang butanding usa ka namingaw nga mananap, busa kinahanglan natong amping-an ug dili gub-on ang puy-anan niini.

findings.note: EN: "The whale shark is an endangered animal". BIS body: "usa ka namingaw nga mananap" = a lonely/desolate animal, and namingaw is the emph_bis word, so it is the highlighted claim. A child reads that the butanding is lonely, not at risk of disappearing. namingaw appears nowhere else in the corpus; the correct word (nameligro) is used in the neighbouring card ffct-02586 and even in this card's own title.

fact_en: Your body is a great healer! When you get a small cut, blood quickly forms a scab to cover it, while new skin grows underneath until it's fully healed.
fact_bis: Maayo kaayo mo-ayo ang imong lawas! Kung adunay samad, dali nga mohimo ang dugo og kugan nga tabon, samtang ang bag-ong panit magtubo sa ilawom hangtod maayo na gyud.

findings.note: title_bis "Samad Lawas Ayaw" — ayaw means "don't"; the intended word is ayo (heal). EN title is "Skin Heals Its Cuts", so the headline reads as a prohibition about wounds instead of a healing fact. Corpus shows the same heal->ayaw title slip at ffct-03304 ("Slow Healing Wounds" -> "Hinay Ayaw Samad") and ffct-05051, versus the correct "Pag-ayo" at ffct-01372.

fact_en: A tortoise moves slowly because its shell is heavy and its legs are short.
fact_bis: Hinay molakaw ang tortoise kay bug-at ang bao niini ug mubo ang mga tiil.

findings.note: title_bis "Hinay nga Pawikan sa Yuta" names a sea turtle (pawikan) for a land tortoise, and the card is specifically about walking on LAND - the exact land/sea distinction the wrong word destroys. The body never gives a Cebuano name for the animal (it leaves "tortoise" in English: "Hinay molakaw ang tortoise kay bug-at ang bao niini"), so a Cebuano-only grade-5 reader takes pawikan as the referent and learns that a sea turtle is the slow land-walker. In Cebuano the land turtle is bao; pawikan is strictly the marine turtle.

fact_en: It takes your stomach a few hours to break down food after a meal — eating regularly keeps a steady supply of energy coming for your body.
fact_bis: Mokabat og pipila ka oras una matunaw sa tiyan ang pagkaon human mokaon — ang regular nga pagkaon naghatag og padayon nga kusog sa lawas.

findings.note: title_bis 'Tulman Oras Tunaw Kaon' for 'Stomach Takes Hours': 'Tulman' is not a word (nearest real word is 'tul-an' = bone, which is off-topic for a stomach card). Rest of the title carries hours/digest/food; body is correct.

fact_en:
Why do lips tingle first from pufferfish poison?

When someone is poisoned by pufferfish, their lips and tongue often tingle or go numb first, because the poison quickly hits the nerves there.
fact_bis:
Nganong mamanhid una ang ngabil sa hilo sa butete?

Kung mahiloan sa butete, ang kasagarang unang mabati mao ang pagkamanhid sa ngabil ug dila, kay dali kaayong maapektuhan sa hilo ang mga nerbiyo didto.

findings.note: title_bis 'Ngabil Mangungmnt Butete': 'Mangungmnt' is not a Cebuano (or any) word — corrupt token, unreadable. The body answers the question correctly, so the fact survives, but the shipped title is broken.

fact_en:
Which joint moves in the most directions?

The ball-and-socket joint gives your body its widest range of motion because it can rotate in many directions.
fact_bis:
Unsang lutahan ang labing lapad molihok?

Ang lutahang bola-ug-lungag naghatag sa pinakalapad nga lihok sa lawas tungod kay makatuyok kini sa daghang direksyon.

findings.note: title_bis 'Bola Lukong Sakit' for 'Ball-and-Socket Joint': 'sakit' means pain/illness and appears nowhere in the card (body is about the joint's range of motion) and 'lutahan' (joint) is missing, so the title announces a card about joint PAIN. Body itself is correct.

fact_en: Inside a joint, smooth cartilage acts like a cushion, so the bones glide instead of rubbing directly against each other.
fact_bis: Sa sulod sa lutahan, adunay hamis nga kartilago nga sama sa unlan, mao nga nagdulhog ang mga bukog imbes nga direktang magkutkot.

findings.note: title_bis 'Cartilage Sakit Buki' for 'Joint Cartilage Cushion': again injects 'sakit' (pain), which the card never mentions, and 'Buki' is not a word (apparently a broken 'bukog'). Title reads as cartilage pain rather than cartilage as a cushion; body is fine.

fact_en:
What's the science of tree rings called?

Studying tree rings to find out a tree's age and the dates it lived through is called dendrochronology.
fact_bis:
Unsa ang pagtuon sa singsing sa kahoy?

Ang pagtuon sa mga singsing sa kahoy aron mahibaw-an ang gulang ug petsa niini gitawag og dendrochronology.

findings.note: title_bis 'Siyensya sa Tree Rin': 'Rin' is a truncated 'Ring' — broken token in a shipped title. Low severity: body uses 'singsing sa kahoy' correctly.

fact_en:
Is abaca related to the banana?

Yes! Abaca and banana both belong to the Musa family — but abaca is grown for its fiber, not its fruit.
fact_bis:
Paryente ba sa saging ang abaka?

Oo! Parehas sila sa pamilyang Musa ang abaka ug saging — apan ang abaka gitanom para sa hilo, dili sa prutas.

findings.note: "ang abaka gitanom para sa hilo, dili sa prutas" — EN is "grown for its fiber". In Cebuano `hilo` reads as POISON (this same batch uses it that way in ffct-03024 liver `mga hilo`, ffct-03099 `hilo sa putyukan` = venom, ffct-03080 `makahilo`). Nothing in the card restores fiber (`lanot`), so the child learns abaca is grown for poison. Flagging despite the thread sense of hílu, because the corpus itself uses hilo = poison.

fact_en: The lion is a big meat-eating predator cat that hunts animals like zebras, antelope, and wild buffalo!
fact_bis: Ang leon usa ka dakong manunukob nga iring nga mokaon lamang og karne — mangayam kini og zebra, antelope, ug ihalas nga kalabaw!

findings.note: title_bis "Leon nga Daku nga Iro" for title_en "The Lion the Great Cat" — `iro` is DOG. The body correctly says `iring` (cat), but the headline itself asserts the lion is a big dog. Same defect class as the known cat-titled-with-iro example.
